| SPN.006 | Switch should support for different logical interface types like loopback, VLAN, SVI/RVI, Port Channel, multi chassis port channel/LAG etc.  |                                                                                                                                                                                                               |                     |                      |
| SPN.007 | The switch should support 32K IPv4 unicast routes and 24K IPv6 unicast routes entries in the routing table including 64,000 multicast routes |                                                                                                                                                                                                               |                     |                      |
| SPN.008 | The switch should support hardware-based load sharing at wire speed using LACP and multi chassis ether channel/LAG                           |                                                                                                                                                                                                               |                     |                      |
| SPN.009 | Switch should support minimum 4 Tbps of switching capacity                                                                                   |                                                                                                                                                                                                               |                     |                      |
| SPN.010 | Layer2 Features                                                                                                                              | Spanning Tree Protocol (IEEE 8201.D, 802.1W, 802.1S)                                                                                                                                                          |                     |                      |
| SPN.011 | Switch should support minimum 32K no. of MAC addresses                                                                                       |                                                                                                                                                                                                               |                     |                      |
| SPN.012 | Switch should support 8 Nos. of link or more per Port channel (using LACP) and support 64 number of ports per Link Aggregation Group         |                                                                                                                                                                                                               |                     |                      |
| SPN.013 |                                                                                                                                              | Support for broadcast, multicast and unknown unicast storm control to prevent degradation of switch performance from storm due to network attacks and vulnerabilities                                         |                     |                      |
| SPN.014 |                                                                                                                                              | The Switch should Multihoming ESI-LAG                                                                                                                                                                         |                     |                      |
| SPN.015 | \*\*Virtualization Features\*\*                                                                                                              | Switch should support Network Virtualisation using Virtual Over Lay Network using VXLAN/ NVGRE or alternative- Optional                                                                                       |                     |                      |
| SPN.016 |                                                                                                                                              | Switch should support VXLAN LAN & EVPN for supporting Spine - Leaf architecture to optimise the east- west traffic flow inside the data center or alternative- Optional                                       |                     |                      |
| SPN.017 | \*\*Layer3 Features\*\*                                                                                                                      | Switch should support static and dynamic routing like Static, OSPF and BGP                                                                                                                                    |                     |                      |
| SPN.018 |                                                                                                                                              | Should support BGP for IPv4 and IPv6                                                                                                                                                                          |                     |                      |

| SPN.022 |                                                                                                                                              | Switch should support for BFD For Fast Failure Detection                                                                                                                                                      |                     |                      |

|         |                                                                                                                                              | and IP V6 and logging for fault finding and audit trail                                                                                                                                                       |                     |                      |

| SPN.035 |                                                                                                                                              | Switch should support central time server synchronization using Network Time Protocol NTP V4                                                                                                                  |                     |                      |

## Primary Storage

**Note:**

* Minimum Primary Storage requirement (Usable) at Data Centre is 3 PB, Secondary Storage requirement at Data Centre (Usable) is 1 PB and Minimum Primary Storage requirement (Usable) at Data Centre for Community Surveillance is 2 PB. Bidder is expected to carry out the storage requirement estimation and supply as per the solution proposed, if the estimation is more than above specified.

* Bidder should also quote for additional Storage in the commercial Schedule.

* If during implementation or O&M, there is any shortage in Storage than MSI need to arrange and procure without any additional cost to NOIDA.

* MSI would be warned and ad-hoc penalty would be applied if any policies (camera resolution, backup etc.) are violated during the project phase.

## Backup Solution

| S.No. | Minimum Requirement Description                                                                                                                                                                                      | Compliance (Yes/No) | Deviations / Remarks |
| ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | -------------------- |
| 1     | The backup solution should be able to create backup relation between primary primary & secondary storage as D2D based backup.                                                                                        |                     |                      |
| 2     | Solution should be highly efficient, point-in-time backup based copies from a solution fully integrated with primary & secondary storage.                                                                            |                     |                      |
| 3     | Solution should be able to Reduce backup times to minutes, even for petabytes of data after first backup.                                                                                                            |                     |                      |
| 4     | Solution should be able to do native format backups enable end user to restore and provide fast application and virtual machine recovery, including industry leading capability to failover to a local Snapshot copy |                     |                      |
| 5     | Solution should be able to transfer only new or changed blocks, compressed to minimize network traffic.                                                                                                              |                     |                      |
| 6     | Solution should be able to reduce data by De-duplication reduces to 90%.                                                                                                                                             |                     |                      |
| 7     | The solution should provide disk to disk based backup to finish in minutes.                                                                                                                                          |                     |                      |
| 8     | Each backup should be block-level incremental but represents a full backup from a restore perspective.                                                                                                               |                     |                      |
| 9     | Solution should be able to integrate with key applications such as Microsoft Exchange, SharePoint, and SQL Server, Oracle, SAP, and virtual infrastructure allows fast, application-consistent recoveries            |                     |                      |
| 10    | The backup solution should be WORM compliant                                                                                                                                                                         |                     |                      |
| 11    | The backup solution should have event based retention.                                                                                                                                                               |                     |                      |
| 12    | The backup solution should have legal hold as a feature by which files can be held in a tamper-proof state for an indefinite time period for litigation purposes                                                     |                     |                      |

| EMS.008 | Network Performance Management                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | The proposed solution platform shall provide a single integrated solution for comprehensive management of the network, routers, servers, cameras and rich visibility into connectivity and performance issues                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |                       |                      |
| EMS.009 |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | The EMS must have Performance Monitoring, Performance Management Control, and Traffic Analysis based upon netflow for network elements.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |                       |                      |
| EMS.010 |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Traffic monitoring should collect and analyse network traffic patterns to provide with real-time traffic utilization and bandwidth usage The module should monitor network flows. to identify traffic like Top Talkers, IP to IP traffic, monitor the bandwidth. The solution will also monitor the port utilization, in/out packets and interface stats to monitor the health of the system. The tool should Dive deep into network traffic patterns, gain actionable insights, and optimize performance to empower the network with data-driven decision-making.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |                       |                      |
| EMS.011 |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | The EMS should conduct the monitoring and management of the coordinated configuration of multiple network devices. Should have Centralized Automation at Scale with Ansible-powered Network Automation. Intelligent Network Device Configuration Management to in control of your network infrastructure by Effortlessly performing backups, compare configurations, and ensure compliance with regulatory standards. It should allow to perform configuration backup of routers, switches, comparison of configuration across devices, line-by-line comparison, in-line comparison. It should allows to define playbooks for configuration. Perform configuration on single device as well as host group.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |                       |                      |
| EMS.012 |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | The EMS must ensure FCAPS monitoring, Fault Management, Network Configuration Management, Network & Server Performance Management across the associated elements in the network.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |                       |                      |
| EMS.013 |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | The proposed solution must provide comprehensive and integrated management of IT infrastructure components to maximize the availability of IT services and SLA performance.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |                       |                      |
| EMS.014 |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | The proposed solution must provide the complete view of the Topology and network elements. The NMS shall have the ability to include the network elements and the links in the visual/graphical map of the department. The visual maps shall display the elements in different color depending upon the status of the element. Should have automated network topology and host Discovery without manual mapping of network, empowering with real-time visibility into network infrastructure with up-to-date network insights. The topology should provide details of neighbors , neighbor IP, neighbor interface, statistics, device kpi on the screen, device vendor, model. The topology should show Traffic utilization, interface status status & details on hovering the mouse over the link/interface. The topology should be able to download in pdf, png, svg format. It should allow to create custom topology, show label and legends. Custom topology should also have bulk upload feature. The topology view should have device name & ip search feature and the device/ip should be highlighted upon search. |                       |                      |
| EMS.015 |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | The proposed solution must keep historical data for minimum 3 months.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |                       |                      |
| EMS.016 |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Proposed EMS/NMS software application should have qualified Security verification certificate by STQC (Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology) or any other Government agency from the list of CERT-IN empaneled Information Security Auditing organization or CIS Certification for testing and issuing the certificate /clearance.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |                       |                      |
| EMS.017 |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Intelligent forecasting should allow advanced planning and forecasting capabilities. Leverage historical data, predictive analytics, and intelligent algorithms to accurately anticipate device metrics such as CPU, disk, and memory usage. Ensure optimal resource allocation, proactively identify capacity bottlenecks, and eliminate performance degradation risks.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |                       |                      |
| EMS.018 |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | The tool should provide unparalleled visibility into the network and infrastructure, Identify trends, patterns, and anomalies related to host and service problems. ## 6.9. Disaster Recovery Service (for future scope)

In the current scope of the Project, **Disaster Recovery Services** is not part of the Scope. Although, in future if there is a need and requirement, Noida Authority may decide to setup Disaster Recovery Service directing the Selected Bidder to setup DR centre at any location with the collaboration of NIC or MeITY empanelled vendors then the MSI can on board with all necessary support, API handshakes for successfully setting up of DR centre by Noida authority. All costs for setting up of DR will be borne by Noida Authority including point to point connectivity from current data centre to DR centre elsewhere.

The Disaster Recovery Centre is a mirror image of all the application hosted at the data center  data center & will be 50% of the Compute however the data of video feeds is to be 100% available in case of Disaster. In case of non-availability of data center, the DR center should be able to operate all the applications of the safe city components. The DR center will have all the functionality and infrastructure like the data centre.

Disaster Recovery Centre will be 50% of Data Centre Site, it is mandatory to have two separate physical location and distance itself through Seismic Zones.

Noida Safe City Project – Volume 2 – Scope of Work 217

![Noida logo](page_218_image_1_v2.jpg)

For Disaster Recovery as a Service, MSI need to ensure it follows the below guidelines:

1) MSI shall avail hosting services from NIC or MEITY Empanelled Cloud Service Provider or State Data Centre to host DR site in addition to implement and manage the architecture accordingly.

2) MSI is responsible for Disaster Recovery Services so as to ensure continuity of operations in the event of failure of primary data centre meet the RPO (Recovery Point Objective) and RTO (Recovery Time Objective) requirements.

3) RPO should be less than or equal to 1 hour i.e. the replication cycle should run at maximum 1 hour that needs to reconsidered as it will be dependent on application to application.

4) RTO shall be less than or equal to 4 hours.

5) During the change from Primary DC to DR or vice-versa (regular planned changes), there should not be any data loss.

6) Support for synchronous and asynchronous data replication.

7) Automated site to site failover and failback.

8) Support for non-identical server and storage configurations at the remote site.

9) The Primary Managed hosted DC-DR should be in different seismic zones.

10) MSI should provision VM’s for both DC and DR.

11) During normal operations, the Primary Data Centre will serve the requests. The Disaster Recovery Site shall will not be performing any work but will remain on standby.

12) During this period, the compute environment for the application in DR shall be available on demand basis for a functional DR and minimum compute if required, as per the solution offered. The application environment shall be installed and ready for use.

13) DC Data shall be replicated on an ongoing basis at DR, as per designed RTO/RPO and replication strategy, data consistency and integrity should be maintained

14) Database should be in Active mode at DC and Passive mode at DR, data consistency and integrity should be maintained.

15) In the event of a site failover or switchover, DR site will take over the active role, and all the requests will be routed through that site. Application data and application states will be replicated between data centres so that when an outage occurs, failover to the surviving data centre can be accomplished within the specified RTO. This is the period during which the Compute environment for the application shall be equivalent to DC. The installed application instance and the database shall be usable and the same SLAs as DC shall be provided. The use of this Full Compute DR environment can be for specific periods during a year for the purposes of DC failure or DR Drills or DC maintenance or DC Major Software Upgrades or DC High Peak Load Support.

16) Self-remediating security implementation which allows systems to revert to approved security state at designated interval.

17) Website and live application (both external and internal) should be routed seamlessly from DC site to DR site.

18) The MSI shall conduct DR drill one in every six months, of operation wherein the Primary DC must be deactivated and complete operations shall be carried out from the DR Site. However, during the change from DC to DR or vice-versa (or regular planned changes), there should not be any data loss.

Noida Safe City Project – Volume 2 – Scope of Work 218

![Noida logo](page_219_image_1_v2.jpg)

19) The MSI shall clearly define the procedure for announcing DR based on the proposed DR solution. The MSI shall also clearly specify the situations in which disaster shall be announced along with the implications of disaster and the time frame required for migrating to DR. The MSI shall plan all the activities to be carried out during the Disaster Drill and issue a notice to the Department at least 15 working days before such drill.

20) RPO monitoring, Reporting and Events Analytics for the Disaster recovery solutions should be offered as part of the offering. Any lag in data replication should be clearly visible in dashboard and alerts of same should be sent to respective authorities.

21) Training should be provided to the staff members and System Administrator on DR.

22) Services provider should provide the solution document of DR.

23) Selected bidder should have proper escalation procedure and emergency response in case of failure/disaster at DC.

24) Selected bidder shall provide support for all server maintenance activities. This would include periodic health check, on-demand troubleshooting, etc. from certified vendors. ITIL processes named problem, change, incident & configuration will be followed by selected bidder at DR site.

25) Selected bidder shall provide Disaster Recovery services during the event of Disaster.

26) The Selected bidder shall configure all the components and sub-components for end-to end user access to all Windows applications/services.

27) The Selected bidder will have to demonstrate the DR site to run on thirty percent capacity for proving successful implementation of the DR site.

28) Noida reserves the right, on its own or via a third-party auditor, to conduct overall testing at any point of time for the services delivered by the selected bidder.

29) The Service Provider shall make provisioning of requisite software licenses, Database licenses and other required monitoring software, tools for IT setup at DR site

30) The Service Provider shall undertake installation and configuration of operating systems, databases, and storage solution and replication mechanism for all in-scope business application systems.

31) The selected bidder shall undertake installation and configuration of any other specialized applications/ software solution/Hardware solution required for the Disaster Recovery Setup.

32) The selected bidder would be solely responsible for implementation of all applications at DR site. All costs including licenses for application, OS, replication tools or databases if any shall be borne by the service provider

33) Automated switchover/ failover facilities (during DC failure & DR Drills) to be provided and ensured by selected bidder. The switchback mechanism shall also be automated. The selected bidder shall also provide a tool/ mechanism for DC to trigger DR switchover.

34) Selected bidder shall provide support for the development of detailed activity plans for recovery for all systems.

35) Selected bidder shall provide support for the development of a detailed disaster recovery plan. This plan document will contain steps/procedures to switch over services to DR site in the event of invocation of disaster at DC site. Selected bidder shall also document steps for restoring services from DR site to DC site.

36) Selected bidder shall provide support with the development of detailed operating manuals for the implemented replication solution from system administrator’s perspective.

2) Fiber network deployed for the city should be underground and overhead shall be entertained only on specific request and approval from NOIDA. All the equipment i.e., network, power etc. and manpower services for trenching, cable blowing, ducting etc. involved would be within the scope of MSI.
3) MSI shall use Radio Frequency (RF) transmission on confirmation from NOIDA for selected / secluded places only for communication between field devices infrastructure to the core router through existing Internet Service Provider or Telecom Service Provider (ISP / TSP). Required security applications should be factored in to avoid hacks at field devices infrastructure level.
4) MSI should estimate the bandwidth requirement for connectivity to desired DC and the same shall be clearly provisioned in the technical proposal with detailed calculations.
5) Connectivity between ICCC and Data Centre shall be mentioned explicitly and approved from NOIDA.
6) Bandwidth provisioned needs to adhere to following minimum benchmark requirements:
    I. Latency should be less than 15 ms
    II. Jitter should be less than 2% of one-way latency
    III. Packet loss should be less than 0.01%
7) MSI shall meet the parameters of video feed quality, security & performance. MSI should factor the same while designing the solution.

### 7.2. Functional Requirement

#### Aggregation and Pre-Aggregation Layer

*   Aggregation routers are sent to terminate the Pre-Aggregation rings. Aggregation & Pre- Aggregation node will be layer-3 capable device with IP and dual stack support (Ipv4 and Ipv6).
*   Aggregation & Pre-Aggregation layer should be considered with following:
    *   2x10Gig bandwidth for core ring with the help of Aggregation Routers, 10G LR SFP+ modules shall be considered for this ring design, which can go up-to 10 Kms
    *   Nx1G Ring would be considered for Aggregation ring which would be formed using Pre- Aggregation Node. 1G Long haul SM modules will be used for this ring.
    *   HQoS (shaping with nested policy maps) support
    *   Multi-VLAN support (802.1q)
    *   Standard Routing protocols (IS-IS, BGP)

#### Core Layer

Core node will be the Core layer i.e., IP City Network.
Following should be functional requirements for Core layer discussion.

• There will be two numbers of Core nodes and are placed in the DC

• These core routers will connect to DC Spine-leaf switches over 1x10Gbps connectivity

• Layer-3 with 6PE, 6VPE

• Dual stack support (IPv4/IPv6)

## City Network Features

Functional requirements and key design parameters of the network:

• The network will be built to provide the following:

• Higher Network Uptime

• Visibility of Network

• Better Utilization of WAN Links

• Segregation of Traffic and QOS

• Better Network Management

1. The network will have the capability and facility for seamless integration with all other components required to build backbone Network

2. Network will act as Backbone for all the City services, which may come in future.

3. Network must support next generation architecture to support next-gen application like Voice, Video, Wi-Fi etc in future.

4. Network will be connected in Ring fashion and the proposed devices support redundancy Protocol like MPLS-TE for better convergence.

5. The Ring Based architecture must be deployed to meet the following:

• Redundancy of nodes and Links

• Less prone to failures

• Better Link utilization

• Easy Insertion of new Node. No configuration change at Core

6. Network must support Node and Link protection feature for faster and reliable network convergence. The following criteria are required to be ensured:

• Optimized utilization of redundant links

• Un-even utilization of links

• The Network must support MPLS QoS features.

• All devices will support priority queuing for assigning more priority to Video traffic over non-critical data traffic.

## High Availability in Network

High Availability technology helps to facilitate network-wide resilience to increase IP network availability. It provides continuous access to applications, data, and content anywhere, anytime by addressing potential causes of downtime with functionality, design, and best practices.

At a top level, high availability can be segmented in following two categories:

• Physical layer

• Logical layer

Noida Safe City Project – Volume 2 – Scope of Work 221

![Noida logo](page_222_image_1_v2.jpg)

## Physical layer

Some of the components which improves hardware level network high availability are-
* Redundant Core Router at Data centre (existing)
* Additionally, Dual Supervisor engines/power/fans at Core/Backbone router
* Hot-swappable Modules/fans in Core/Aggregation Router
* Fiber design and Links level redundancy

## Logical layer

Fast Reroute: Fast Reroute (FRR) mechanism must be deployed to protect traffic engineering (TE) LSPs from link and node failures by locally repairing the LSPs at the point of failure and allowing data to continue to flow on them while the head end routers attempt to establish new end-to-end LSPs. FRR will be deployed to locally repair the protected LSPs by rerouting them over backup tunnels that bypass failed links or node.

## Link Protection

Backup tunnels will be created to bypass only a single link of the LSP’s path for providing link protection. This will protect LSPs if a link along their path fails by rerouting the LSP’s traffic to the next hop (bypassing the failed link).

## Node Protection

FRR will be deployed to provide node protection for LSPs. Backup tunnels that bypass next-hop nodes along LSP paths (NNHOP) will be deployed as backup tunnels to protect the primary tunnels. The backup tunnel will protect LSPs if a node along their path fails by enabling the node upstream of the failure to reroute the LSPs and their traffic around the failed node to the next- next hop. FRR must support the use of RSVP Hellos to accelerate the detection of node failures.

## REP/G.8032 or Equivalent Ring Protection:

REP or Equivalent will be used in the access layer to provide faster convergence in case of link or node failure.

## B. Installation of HDPE Pipes

*   The MSI shall lay 1 number of 25/40mm HDPE pipes for this Network
*   The MSI shall decoil 25/40 mm HDPE pipe with the help of Mechanical Decoilers.
*   The MSI shall lay 25/40 mm HDPE Pipe in a flat bottom trench-free from stones, sharp edged debris. Wherever stones or sharp-edged debris exist, sand bedding of 50 mm thickness shall be prepared on which the 25/40 mm HDPE pipes shall be laid.
*   The MSI shall ensure minimum bending radius of pipe and fibre optic cable.
*   The MSI shall use end plugs to close the pipe openings to avoid ingress of mud, water, or dust.
*   The MSI shall use HDPE couplers as per joint.
*   The MSI shall use duct spacers to protect ducts from crossing each other inside the trench.
*   The MSI shall test the continuity of HDPE pipes as per the Duct Integrity test for all ducts.

## C. Installation of DWC Pipes

*   The MSI shall use suitable DWC pipe to facilitate adequate protection to 25/40 mm HDPE pipe and OFC within low depth areas (as specified in Table above) as well as at rail, road, bridge, and culvert crossings.
*   The MSI shall use DWC coupler to joint DWC pipe.
*   The MSI shall lay DWC pipe on levelled bed of trench.
*   The MSI shall ensure that the trench bed is free from sharp edge and debris and stones.

## D. Installation of GI Pipes

*   The MSI shall lay GI pipe wherever road and culvert crossings are encountered on the route as well as in depth areas.
*   The MSI shall clamp GI Pipe with suitable clamps where ever culvert crossing is to be done and excavation is not possible. The 25/40mm HDPE Pipes shall be laid through GI Pipe.
*   The MSI shall build a box culvert to protect GI Pipe in case of lower depth.
*   The MSI shall extend the GI pipe by at least 1 meter on each side of crossing subject to availability of space.
*   The SI shall join GI pipes using suitable GI Coupler.

## E. Protection for OFC

*   The Optical Fiber Network shall be built by considering following protection methods to protect the OFC from accidental damage.
*   Concreting: Concreting shall be used to provide additional protection on bridges, Culverts and on stretches wherever depth of excavation is less than 0.2Mtr.
*   RCC Half round: Where-ever cables are laid in cities, towns, and villages where human habitation exists or where construction activity can happen in near future, Full Round or Half Round, 100mm, NP2 Grade shall be put after 100mm padding with excavated material over duct, wherever the depth is less than 0.5Mtr but more than 0.4Mtr.

7.4.4. *Optical Fibre Cable Testing Methodology*

The procedure shall comply with the inspection/IEC 14763-3 standard and to the vendor testing procedure.

The ISO/IEC 14763 standard specifies the implementation and operation of Noida premises cabling.

Tests applied to links and exclude equipment and work area cord.

OF Attenuation testing is used to verify the initial performance of the installed link. 100 % of the installed OF links have to be tested and must pass the acceptance criteria.

The attenuation of the link is measured using the insertion loss method. This method uses an optical source and an optical power meter to compare the difference between two optical power levels.

When testing Single Mode optical fibre links with a Light Source and a Power Meter, this measurement kit must be capable of operating at 1550 nm and 1310 nm for Single Mode.

The test scenario with a Light Source and a Power Meter shall be of the following for each link: Bidirectional testing @ 1550 nm and @ 1310 nm for single mode fibres and calculating average of both readings.

The use of certification tool is recommended. Those tools can produce a report logging the time of the test the link identification under test, the link length, the attenuation at the window tested and the acceptable link attenuation. The report shall also identify in which direction the testing was implemented.

When testing with basic optical source and power meter, the operator will fill up a report logging the time of the test, the link identification under test, the link length and attenuation at the window tested in presence of the deputed staff/any person by Noida.

The report shall also identify in which direction the testing was implemented.

Acceptance link attenuation/loss in dB per link (between 2 locations) to be calculated as per below.

Noida Safe City Project – Volume 2 – Scope of Work 232

![Noida logo](page_233_image_1_v2.jpg)

- For 1310 nm: 0.34 dB attenuation / Km + 0.05 dB / splice + 1 dB connector loss
- For 1550 nm: 0.20 dB attenuation / Km + 0.05 dB / splice + 1 dB connector loss

MSI shall also be responsible to replace a patch of OFC cable for suitable length if optical losses are increased due to added splice joints etc., which may result in below conditions.

Any of the SLA is violated.

Performance of link is deteriorated with respect to user service.

Link is not getting up due to increased losses. The measured attenuation of the links shall have a lower value than the acceptable link attenuation calculated.

The Test should be carried out by certified Engineer and once the report is submitted to the manufacturer, he will issue the Performance Certification which will mention minimum performance of 10 years or higher.

The MSI shall also provide bidirectional OTDR report for all fibre cores.

### <span style="color:red">7.4.5.</span> <span style="color:red; font-style:italic;">Earthing System</span>

All electrical components are to be earthen by connecting two earth tapes from the frame of the component ring and will be connected via several earth electrodes. The cable arm will be earthen through the cable glands. The entire applicable IT infrastructure shall have adequate earthing.

Further, earthling should be done as per Local state national standard in relevance with IS standard.

Earthing should be done for the entire power system and provisioning should be there to earth UPS systems, Power distribution units, AC units, etc. to avoid a ground differential.

All metallic objects on the premises that are likely to be energized by electric currents should be effectively grounded.

## 8. COMPONENT 5: City Model and Digital Twin Technology

### 8.1. Overview

This project aims to deliver a high-quality Digital Twin Platform of the Area of Interest (AOI) i.e., 225 Sq. Km of Noida that brings revolutionary clarity in the geospatial understanding of an environment.

3D Digital Twin Platform would be an advanced and immersive platform integrated with command-and-control center platform and 3D GIS technology into the existing Safe city infrastructure. This solution combines real-time data, geospatial information, and immersive 3D visualization to enhance the management, monitoring, and decision-making processes within the city.

Key Components and Features:

1. **3D GIS Platform:** Develop a state-of-the-art 3D GIS platform that serves as the foundation for the ICCC. This platform should integrate seamlessly with existing city systems and databases.
2. **Immersive Visualization:** Implement 3D visualization technologies, such as virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR), to provide a more immersive and interactive experience for operators. This allows them to explore the city in 3D, zoom in on specific areas, and view real-time data overlays.
3. **Real-time Data Integration:** Integrate data from various sources, including IoT sensors, surveillance cameras, weather stations, traffic sensors, public safety systems, and utility networks. This data should be displayed on the 3D map in real time.
4. **Geospatial Analytics:** Utilize geospatial analytics to analyze data, identify trends, and predict events. For example, it can help in predicting traffic congestion, monitoring air quality, or identifying areas at risk of flooding.
5. **Scenario Simulation:** Create a feature that allows operators to simulate different scenarios, such as natural disasters, traffic accidents, or crowd management during events. This can help in planning and training for emergency responses.
6. **Emergency Response Coordination:** In case of emergencies, the 3D Digital Twin Platform can streamline the coordination of various agencies (police, fire, medical services) by providing a real-time, 3D views of the incident and its impact on the city.
7. **Public Engagement:** Offer a public-facing interface or mobile application that provides residents with access to 3D maps and real-time information about events, traffic, and city services. This promotes transparency and encourages community involvement in public safety and city management.
8. **Augmented Reality Field Operations:** Equip field personnel, such as first responders or utility workers, with augmented reality devices that overlay critical information on their field of view, making their tasks more efficient and safer.
9. **Data Security and Privacy:** Implement robust cybersecurity measures to protect sensitive data and ensure compliance with privacy regulations.
10. **Scalability:** Design the system to be scalable, so it can accommodate the growing needs of a smart and safe city and adapt to technological advancements, Artificial Intelligence for assisted operations.
11. **Public Transport Planning:** Enhance public transport based on the demand and surges. This will increase the overall quality of life of citizens by providing easy transport, reduction in carbon foot print and increased efficiency.

13. Utility Planning: Simulate energy, water, and waste management systems to improve resource allocation and sustainability.

14. Traffic Management: Create free moving paths for services like ambulance, fire fighters and police

15. Digital Surveillance: Flag potential risky behaviors without compromising privacy of the citizens

16. Digital Tourism: An interactive experience for tourist to explore and navigate the city.

The City 3D Digital Twin solution aims to revolutionize urban management by providing holistic 3D experiences of the city's operations. It enables proactive decision-making, better resource allocation, and improved public safety while fostering a more engaged and informed community.

By integrating these technologies and approaches, cities can enhance their ability to prevent and respond to public safety issues, ultimately making urban environments safer for their residents and visitors.

### 8.3.2.2. Survey Methodology

Executing a LiDAR survey with a mobile system to determine optimal camera pole positions follows a structured process designed to secure precise data gathering and location evaluation. This approach can be delineated into multiple phases:

a) Planning:

- Precisely define the survey's objectives, including the intended use for camera pole placement, such as enhancing safe city surveillance, monitoring traffic, or facilitating urban planning.

- Choose the survey location carefully, considering factors such as urban population density, crime rates, traffic flow, and infrastructure requirements.

- Verify that all essential permits and authorizations have been secured to carry out the mobile LiDAR survey.

b) Setting up the LiDAR System:

- LiDAR Sensor Selection: Select a suitable LiDAR sensor based on the survey's range, accuracy, and point cloud density prerequisites.

- Mobile LiDAR Vehicle Preparation: Equip a vehicle with the LiDAR system, high-precision GPS, IMU, and, if needed, cameras for data acquisition.

- Calibration: Precisely calibrate the LiDAR system to guarantee accurate data capture and synchronization with the GPS and IMU.

c) Data Gathering:

- Route Planning: Strategically plan the survey route within the designated area, considering road accessibility and ensuring the safety of the survey vehicle.

- Data collection: Operate the mobile LiDAR vehicle within the survey area, acquiring LiDAR point cloud data and precisely georeferencing it using GPS and IMU data.

- Camera Pole Location Criteria: Establish the criteria for identifying suitable camera pole sites, considering factors such as visibility, optimal viewing angles, and proximity to critical features or high-risk areas.

- Data Integration: Merge LiDAR data with optional imagery (captured by cameras) to generate a comprehensive dataset.

### 8.3.2.3. Data Processing

a. Point Cloud Registration: Process the LiDAR data to guarantee precise registration and alignment of point clouds acquired from various scans.

b. Object Detection and Classification: Utilize dedicated software to recognize and categorize objects, encompassing poles, structures, trees, vehicles, and pedestrians.

c. Locating Appropriate Sites: Examine the LiDAR data and extracted information to pinpoint potential camera pole sites that adhere to the predefined criteria.

d. Geospatial Assessment: Conduct geospatial analysis to evaluate visibility, coverage, and surveillance angles, ensuring optimal performance.

## 8.3.2.4. Network and Power Planning

1. Integration of Camera Pole Locations into Network Design:
* Utilization of LiDAR Data: The detailed 3D LiDAR point cloud data is harnessed to evaluate proposed camera pole sites, considering factors like line-of-sight visibility, coverage, and surveillance angles. This data forms the basis for informed decision-making.
* GIS Data Integration: Processed LiDAR data is seamlessly integrated into a Geographic Information System (GIS). Within the GIS, camera pole locations are mapped and their attributes, such as height and orientation, are recorded.
* Network Infrastructure Planning: Network planning specialists leverage the GIS data to determine how camera poles can be effectively incorporated into the existing network infrastructure. This includes optimizing the placement of networking equipment, cables, and power components to establish a robust connection between the camera poles and the central command or data centre.

2. Power Requirements and Plans for Camera Pole Locations:
* Power Needs Assessment: The power demands of camera poles are assessed based on variables such as camera types, lighting requirements, and potential auxiliary equipment. LiDAR data assists in evaluating the proximity of power sources, such as utility poles or electrical infrastructure, to the proposed camera pole locations.
* Power Distribution Strategy: Once the power requirements are identified, a comprehensive plan is formulated for the distribution of power to the camera poles. This may involve the installation of power distribution units or connectivity to existing electrical infrastructure.
* Backup Power Contingency: Contingency plans are devised to ensure continuous operation in the event of power outages. Backup power solutions, including uninterruptible power supplies (UPS) or generators, are considered.

### 8.3.2.5. Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QA/QC)

Quality Assurance and Quality Control (QA/QC) Procedures for Mobile LiDAR Survey in Safe City Project ensures Data Accuracy

Ensuring the accuracy and reliability of data in a Mobile LiDAR survey for Safe City Project involves a set of rigorous QA/QC procedures at various stages of the survey. These procedures are in place to maintain data accuracy from data acquisition to the final data output. Here is an overview of the QA/QC processes:

1. Pre-Survey Preparations:
* Define clear survey objectives and establish desired accuracy standards.
* Select suitable, high-precision LiDAR equipment.
* Ensure the readiness and proper functioning of the mobile LiDAR vehicle and its associated systems.

2. Data Acquisition Phase:
* Conduct calibration checks to confirm proper alignment and functionality of sensors.
* Set up ground control points (GCPs) at known locations to enable post-survey accuracy assessments.
* Implement real-time data monitoring with quality checks during data collection to promptly detect any issues.

3. Data Processing Phase:
* Register and align point clouds from various passes to achieve seamless and accurate coverage.
* Apply filtering techniques to remove outliers and noise from the data.
* Conduct classification and feature extraction to accurately identify objects, including camera poles.

4. Accuracy Assessment:
* After processing, compare the LiDAR data with GCPs to assess the overall survey accuracy.
* Evaluate the positional accuracy of detected objects, such as camera pole locations, using ground truth data or independent verification.

5. Data Validation and Verification:
* Review processed data to identify anomalies or inconsistencies.

Noida Safe City Project – Volume 2 – Scope of Work 242

![Noida logo](page_243_image_1_v2.jpg)

- Cross-verify LiDAR-derived information with other data sources (e.g., existing maps or satellite imagery) to ensure data consistency.

6. Documentation:

- Maintain detailed records of all QA/QC activities and their outcomes.

- Document any issues detected and describe the corrective actions taken.

7. Iterative Improvement:

- Establish a feedback loop to address identified issues and refine data processing based on QA/QC findings.

8. Reporting:

- Compile a comprehensive QA/QC report, encompassing information on data accuracy, anomalies, and corrective measures.

- Document any deviations from accuracy standards and outline the steps taken to rectify them.

9. Adherence to Standards:

- Ensure full compliance with industry and project-specific accuracy standards and guidelines.

By following these QA/QC procedures, the Mobile LiDAR survey maintains data accuracy throughout the acquisition and processing phases, guaranteeing the reliability of results for Safe City Project. These measures play a pivotal role in detecting and rectifying errors, ensuring that the survey data meets the specified accuracy requirements.

4.  Data Processing (4-6 weeks):

    *   Register and align point clouds from different survey passes.
    *   Remove noise and outliers from the data through filtering.
    *   Classify and categorize LiDAR data, including object identification (e.g., camera pole locations).
    *   Generate digital elevation models (DEMs) and other derivatives.
    *   Conduct quality control checks during processing.

5.  Accuracy Assessment and QA/QC (2 weeks):
    *   Compare LiDAR data with GCPs to assess overall accuracy.
    *   Evaluate positional accuracy of identified objects.
    *   Review processed data for anomalies and inconsistencies.
    *   Verify data accuracy and consistency with other data sources.

6.  Data Integration and GIS (1-2 weeks):
    *   Integrate processed LiDAR data into a Geographic Information System (GIS).
    *   Create maps and visualizations, including proposed camera pole locations.
    *   Combine LiDAR data with imagery and other relevant GIS-compatible data.

7.  Report Generation (1-2 weeks):
    *   Compile a comprehensive report detailing project specifics, accuracy assessments, and quality control findings.
    *   Present identified camera pole locations and other relevant data.

8.  Final Data Delivery (1-2 weeks):
    *   Provide the client with the final LiDAR data, including point clouds, DEMs, and GIS-compatible files.
    *   Deliver location maps displaying proposed camera pole placements.

### 8.3.2.9. Specifications of Terrestrial / Mobile LiDAR Data / Backpack LiDAR / Panoramic Imaging Sensors

*   Mobile LiDAR Scanner shall have one or more onboard (roving) Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) dual frequency receiver supporting dual antenna configuration.
*   Base Station shall have one or more Static GNSS dual frequency receivers, capable of simultaneous collection and storage of real-time kinematic (RTK) data, and kinematic data that can be post processed.
*   MLS should have tight integration with an IMU (Inertial measurement unit) and distance measurement instrument (DMI).
*   MLS shall be capable of data capturing in 360º coverage angle.

Noida Safe City Project – Volume 2 – Scope of Work 246

![Noida logo](page_247_image_1_v2.jpg)

• System should include multiple sensors mounted in different directions covering 360 Degree view (90% of a sphere) for street view mapping.

• Minimum resolution for each individual sensor should be 12 megapixel or better.

• LiDAR scanner used with the system shall be certified for safety issues (eye safe)

• The GNSS/IMU employed in the system shall meet or exceed the following performance specifications:

▪ Frequency rate of minimum 200 Hz
▪ Track multiple constellations
▪ Accuracy in roll and pitch (RMS): 0.004º
▪ Accuracy in heading (RMS): 0.013º

• Data shall be collected in the time periods with minimum obstacles/traffic present such as early mornings.

• There shall be minimum of 5 satellites required for data collection. However, wherever this is not possible, the bidder shall establish temporary GCPs as necessary.

• Data shall be collected in weather free from cloud/fog.

• GPS Time stamp shall be recorded and delivered for each point

• Reference measurement unit shall be in meters.

• MLS shall be capable of 300 or better points per Square Meters.

• Mobile LiDAR shall be capable to cover 75-meter range on each side of the road.

• Data voids within a single swath shall not be acceptable, except in the below mentioned cases:
    ▪ Water Bodies
    ▪ Areas of low near infrared (NIR) reflectivity, such as asphalt
    ▪ Object shadowing (e.g., buildings, towers, vertical cliffs)

• No point shall be deleted or added in the processing of the data.

• No point shall be classified as raw/ default/never.

• All LAS files header should include geo-referenced information as WKT (well-known text).

## 9. COMPONENT 6: Cyber and Digital Forensics Solutions

### 9.1. Objectives of the Platform

To enable an end-to-end investigation flow that is effective, efficient, and manageable for handling threat and avoiding unwanted accidents during political summit, large events or trade shows, based on a unified investigation platform.

While physical security plays a key role in managing large scale events, gatherings and political summits by identifying possible threats and alarming the security staff, it must be considered that crimes are more complex and increasingly influenced by technology these days. There is a lot of planning and use of technology involved in executing violent attacks and identifying security breaches. At the same time being connected and working as a syndicate for executing such crimes is most common.

Hence it is not enough to identify a suspect in real time and ensure that all safety concerns have been covered. Its most critical to investigate the suspect and try to analyze its movements (locations), connections, planned crime, syndicate and modus operandi.

Our world has never been better connected or more vulnerable. Digital technology is the thread that connects our lives and it is growing at an amazing speed. Mountains of data are being generated and investigating agencies are struggling to cope. Following the data trail to solve crimes is becoming increasingly difficult.

Since digital evidence has become a driving force behind criminal investigations of all types, agencies are rethinking the way their organizations handle digital data. They are seeing the value in implementing a Digital Intelligence (DI) strategy to access, manage, and leverage digital evidence to solve more cases faster and build trust within communities.

The Digital Intelligence Platform assists agencies around the globe to get through the challenges and demands of this Digital investigation.

![Diagram showing interconnected gears labeled People, Processes, Platform, and Policy with associated bullet points](page_251_image_1_v2.jpg)

Noida Safe City Project – Volume 2 – Scope of Work 251

![Noida logo](page_252_image_1_v2.jpg)

At the core of the solution lays the understanding that the challenges of this digital era also bring opportunities. Criminals tend to leave a digital footprint which can provide key answers to key questions that are part of every investigation - Where, When, Who, What, and Why.

Extracting those answers fast and interfacing them to all relevant investigation’s stakeholders by ‘democratizing the data’ is the key to bridging the gap between the volume and complexity of data and the ongoing decrease of resources and expertise.

## 9.2. High Level Requirement

Safety and Security is one of the most critical requirements Noida City. The Noida Authority is planning to have a Command-and-Control Centre (ICCC) for Police department to manage the Law and Order by deploying various key ICT Components in the city, and this state of art CCC would like to address Physical Security components within the premises to address the digital safety and security requirements.

However, with the use of technology and communication its prudent to consider the implementation of a Digital Intelligence Platform which would help to effectively manage the onsite investigations (extract/decode and analyses all the digital information) related to a suspect trying to breach the security or a criminal identified through surveillance etc.

In a possible scenario, while several important and international events occur throughout a year for large industrialist and Noida being a center of attraction for ease of Business, a suspect is apprehended during while trying to sneak into such area with some explosives/unwanted objects.

In another scenario, the Facial Recognition System (FRS) identifies a suspect as blacklisted person as per its database and the suspect is apprehended by the Police.

As per the Standard Operation Procedure (SOP), the suspect will be interrogated by the Police to get insights and leads about his real motive which can be a much bigger conspiracy.

During such situation, there is a need to have a capability which can allow the end customer to successfully extract the digital evidence from the different devices in possession of the suspect, like Mobile Phone, Smart Watch, Laptop, external drives or any other device and his Cloud Applications data.

Once the relevant data is extracted from these multiple devices, there is a need to decode, analyses and validate all essential digital data quickly and effectively. The analysis of this digital data can provide valuable insights like his previous locations, his contacts (with whom he has been communicating/sharing information on various instant messaging/social media platforms), images, videos, emails, documents etc. This digital data can pave way for uncovering lots of other relevant information, based on which timely action will be taken to avoid any untoward incident or situation.

A Digital Intelligence (DI) Platform provides all the above capabilities which include extract, decode, and analyses the digital data.

Noida Safe City Project – Volume 2 – Scope of Work 252

The proposed Digital Intelligence Platform will have the capability to extract, decode and the analyses the decoded digital data.

DI Platform architecture comprises of a selection and integration of proven ‘best in class’ products based on the principles of:

*   Maximize **Data Access** from ever-changing multiple digital data sources, applications and repositories,
*   **Leverage** the big data that is collected for rapid actionable insights,
*   **Manage** the entire investigation and intelligence process to manage the integrity and availability of data.

## 9.3.1.Extraction of Data (Mobile, Computer, Smart Watch, Hard Disk and Cloud)

Complicated locks, encryption barriers, deleted and unknown content, and other obstacles to reviewing device data in addition to capturing and reviewing public domain social media and cloud-based data can prevent critical evidence from coming to light. For investigations to get the fullest picture possible, forensic examiners and investigators need to extract forensically sound data thoroughly and quickly and deliver meaningful insights that help advance the case. The solution provides capability for accessing digital forensics data, with unsurpassed capabilities to extract and decode the most data from the widest range of devices and applications, specifically focusing on mobile devices. With the solution, users can delve deep with comprehensive access to logical, file system and physically extracted data, even hidden and deleted, and discover crucial evidence that can solve a case.

Beyond using social media, web and other cloud-based services to connect, store and share information, people rely on cloud applications to perform day to day activities. This includes shopping online, banking and sometimes hiding behind anonymous user accounts to engage in illicit activities. All this generates a vast amount of data which can be crucial in identifying critical connections, establishing motives and surfacing insights to keep investigations moving forward. Cloud-based sources and the web represent virtual goldmines of potential evidence for investigations. However, acquiring information from private cloud service providers, which requires a warrant, can be a lengthy process for time-sensitive cases. Manually scouring public data from social media is a cumbersome and time-consuming process. Not to mention that analyzing such large volumes of disparate data presents a complex, labor-intensive challenge in and of itself. Producing timely, defensible evidence from cloud and web-based data has the potential to not only speed up investigations, but also solve cases.

The proposed Digital Intelligence solution allows users to extract, preserve and analyze social media data, instant messaging, file storage and other cloud and web-based content from the public and legally pre-approved private sources. With this solution, the users can easily search, filter, sort and share data to quickly identify relevant pieces of information from Cloud Sources.

## 9.3.2. Examining the Digital Data

The platform provides the capability for recovering and examining digital data from the broadest range of digital devices, applications, the cloud and warrant returns. It provides an extensive set of tools and capabilities that allows the examiners to dig deeper into the data and easily surface key evidence. From automatic decryption and decoding to application insights and data validation, this capability is must for any investigation. Application insights and the visual dashboard widgets, an advanced graphical timeline allows to build a storyline of events and zoom in on a specific timeframe of interest. It provides capability to carve unallocated space in a device’s memory to recover deleted data and media files and emulate any Android application using for a more intuitive view of the extracted data. It provides access to the widest range of applications, devices and file formats and reassemble device and application data into readable formats with SQLite Wizard, Python scripting and Hex highlighting.

Noida Safe City Project – Volume 2 – Scope of Work 254

## 9.3.3. Analysis of the Digital Data

Automation of the analysis of digital data to resolve investigations faster is the need of the hour. Digital data can no longer be ignored in modern day investigations. With an ever-growing variety of digital devices and cloud sources producing volumes of highly valuable data, investigators need an intuitive tool to leverage this critical source of evidence when resources are limited.

The proposed Digital Intelligence platform eliminates the time-consuming and manual review of digital data. It is a force multiplier that uses Artificial Intelligence (AI), and machine learning algorithms, to automatically surfaces formative leads and actionable insights from every bit and byte of digital data during the early hours of an investigation by identifying patterns, revealing connections, and uncovering leads with greater speed and accuracy.

When a crime occurs, the race is on to generate leads, identify suspects and make arrests. Case outcomes often rely on digital evidence yet analysing large volumes of disparate data is difficult and time consuming, putting investigations at risk. Forensic practitioners need fast, powerful analytics tools that can turn raw data into intelligence that investigators can act on.

The proposed Digital Intelligence platform provides the capability to automate time-intensive analytical tasks to deliver the deepest, most accurate insights possible and shorten investigation cycles. This capability adds power and value to the existing forensic tools with purpose-built analytical engines that allow users to quickly correlate, analyses and cross reference large disparate sets of mobile, cloud and telco data.

The solution helps to dynamically view data from multiple angles and isolate key details, like objects or faces within images, for easy analysis and reporting to case stakeholders. Investigators benefit from not having to review large, cumbersome PDF reports but instead applying real-time knowledge and context required to work cases faster and keep communities safer. Prosecutors get accurate, defensible intelligence that effectively bolsters their case. It provides capability to establish common links, like Calls, messages, emails, chats, locations patterns between mobile phone users.

Some AI engines that can be used include:

Image categorization- Identify and group images by topics such as nudity, drugs, money, and many more to help investigators focus on the most relevant images. Image categorization is accompanied by CES category which uses cutting-edge neural network algorithms to reveal offensive child exploitation images, and even new ones which are not part of any existing database.

*   Video synopsis
    *   Save crucial time by enabling users to categorize videos automatically and review only the frames within the video that are suspected as identified category.
    *   Image similarity- Find images by similarity, way beyond hash matching, and reveal shared locations and other similarities that may generate new leads.
*   Face detection and face similarity
    *   Search for faces, group them, name them and find similar faces in an endless database of images in seconds. Use images from other resources (police data base, CCTV cameras) to search similar faces within the case.

*   Topic detection- Using new text analysis algorithms, the solution can identify suspected conversations suggesting luring, bullying, violence, and more.
*   Semantic search- The solution enables its users to find evidence and surface insights by using semantic search capabilities. This dramatically expands the user’s capability to find leads even when actual keywords are not available (e.g. user can search for ‘red car’ or ‘sex’ and find images of red cars or words that are related to sex).

ix. Topics – Retrieve events categorized under a specific textual category

x. Image & Video Tags – Retrieve media categorized under a specific media category

xi. Tags - Retrieve events tagged by a user

xii. Watch lists - Retrieve events containing phrases on a specific watch list

xiii. Origins – Retrieve events from a specific application source

xiv. Has Databases – Retrieve events matching a specific hash

xv. States - Retrieve events categorized by current state (intact, deleted or unknown).

xvi. Files – Retrieve events with attachments or files of a defined size

xvii. Locations – Retrieve events with Lat/Long coordinates

xviii. Categorized URLs – View web browsing and bookmarking events according to categories of websites

10. Data, User and Case Management

a. The solution should have a case management capability to allow creation and management of investigative cases:
    i. Authorized users should be able to manually create and remove cases within the system.
    ii. Authorized users should be able to manually add digital evidence to a case.

b. The solution should have a user management capability for the centralized management of users and access by creating dedicated roles and permission schemes to match user needs. The following ability should be available:
    i. Allow creation of new users
    ii. Define different permission-based roles
    iii. Assign different roles to the users
    iv. Define user groups and managing user groups
    v. Restrict access to case data based on permissions.
    vi. Case access restricted to specific users assigned to specific cases.
    vii. User authentication based on username and password. There should be an email-based mechanism for password recovery.

c. The solution should have an inbuilt security mechanism to ensure management of user’s access to data and their authorized actions. It should ensure that user of any type or role does not automatically have the right to view the content of any specific case.
    i. Permission based – Based on a role assigned to a user, the set of permissions to determine what activities the user is authorized to perform.
    ii. Authorized access – based on case creation, a particular user should be provided with access to a case. The user should be able to access only cases he is authorized to access; other cases should not appear for this user.

d. The solution should provide the capability for the users to tag the relevant data:
    i. Users should be able to tag any data artifact or set of data artifacts, so they can be referenced by other users.
    ii. Users should be able to quickly filter and view any tagged data they or other users have created.
    iii. Users should be able to manage tags to create a new tag or remove an existing tag based on their role.

e. The solution should provide the capability to create reports containing key pieces of evidence. There should be a capability to summarize only the important events for deeper analysis:

ii. Allow creation of investigative report in PDF format to present the information in the same way it appears in the system:
    1. Allow users to summarize case findings and present the information in a way that should be understood by multiple stakeholders with varied levels of technical understanding.
    2. Allow users to capture the data with relevant context.
    3. Users should be able to include a specific artifact or event in the report.
    4. Users should be able to take a screenshot of the displayed view and include it in the report.
    5. Users should be able to write descriptions on each screenshot to easily describe the story.
    6. Users should be able to easily drag and drop screenshots into a report.

f. It should also provide a dedicated page/tab to monitor the status of different system jobs running in the system. A view of running, failed, pending, completed and canceled jobs should be available.
g. It should provide the Audit trail capability to log user changes to data in the system, such as adding new evidence, changes in evidence, re-executing enrichments that may alter data appearance, adding or removing tags or comments, and exporting data out of the system.
h. Audit logs should record the occurrence of events, the time at which they occurred, the responsible user or service, and the impacted entity.
