## 10. Testing and Acceptance Procedures

Testing and quality assurance in software development is more rigorous since each component has to be more reliable, if it is to be reused. A system is tested at various stages of development and deployment. For example, each component is tested as a unit for checking the correctness of its own code. The component shall be tested with its dependent components. After final release of the entire set of components, system is tested for the correctness of system functionality. The components shall be tested in simulated production load for performance and load analysis. The MSI along with consortium partners shall be responsible for the testing processes such as **planning** (includes preparing test plans and defining roles and their responsibilities), **preparation** (consists of preparing test specification, test environment and test data) and **execution** (includes testing at various levels like unit level, integration level, system level and production).

### 10.1. Test Plan

Test plans are prepared for each phase of testing. The initial test plan is created during the Project Planning phase. The initial test plan describes who performs which type of testing and when. Ideally master test plan covers all types of test i.e. from unit testing to production testing. The MSI along with consortium partners is expected to submit the test plans to NOIDA for approval. Any changes made to the test plan during the project life cycle should be communicated to NOIDA for approval. Test plans should contain following items:

- Roles and responsibilities of test team
- Approach to testing
- Function testing
- Security testing
- User Interface and reports testing
- Concurrency testing
- Performance and Load testing
- Test Scenarios along with entry and exit criteria
- Test specifications
- Suspension and resumption criteria

### 10.2. Test scenarios

The MSI along with consortium partners should prepare test scenario for each business scenario. A test scenario when executed should fulfil a business requirement as per the scope of business functionality. Test scenarios shall include following:

- Test Specification - During the test specification phase, the test cases are specified. It consists of description of the input, process to be executed and a prediction of output results.

- Test Environment - Component developer does unit testing and integration testing. Integration testing can be delegated to a specialized testing group. Each of the members in the testing group is provided with testing environment according to his/her role and responsibilities. Following is sample testing environment for testing:

  - A workstation

Noida Safe City Project – Volume 2 – Scope of Work 278

![Noida logo](page_279_image_1_v2.jpg)

- A set of tools and applications required on workstation like access to user interface, browser etc.

- Access to centralized document database (where all the project related documents are maintained)

- Access to testing tools and defect logging tools

- Access to the central database or repository for development and unit testing (this database contains sample test data)

- Access to deployed components

- Test Data - Test data is prepared for testing at each stage. The test data should be prepared in such a way that it covers basic path and every alternate path of the code. The basic path and alternate paths are prioritized to capture relevant data. Tools can also be used to generate test data.

## 10.3. Test Execution

The following testing steps are usually employed in the project lifecycle. The MSI along with consortium partners expected to follow these steps.

**Unit Testing:** In unit testing, each piece of code has to be rigorously tested. At this stage testing is done according to the priority of path of code. All the test results are logged in the defect logging tools. After completion of testing, code is corrected for defect logs. This process is iterative till criteria for successful testing is reached.

**Integration Testing:** Upon completion of unit testing, integration testing begins. The purpose is to ensure distinct components of the application still work in accordance to customer requirements. Test sets will be developed with the express purpose of exercising the interfaces between the components. This activity is to be carried out by the Test Team. Integration test will be termed complete when actual results and expected results are either in line or differences are explainable/acceptable based on client input.

**Incremental Integration Testing:** Continuous testing of an application as new functionality is added.

**System Testing:** System testing is performed when all the components are delivered to central repository prior to the release of the software. The testing is done on priority basis of business processes. All the defects are logged and assigned to respective component owners. The component and unit testing shall be performed after the correction of code. However, it may depend on size and type of individual test specifications. Impact analysis is useful to narrow done testing efforts by identifying critical test cases affected due to code change.

**Pre-Production Testing:** Pre-Production testing is done simulating the production load. Test data is either prepared or generated from the tools. This testing is used to evaluate performance, load capacity and concurrency. Load testing tools can also be used for this purpose. Following special type of testing are done during Pre-production Testing Phase:

Noida Safe City Project – Volume 2 – Scope of Work 279

![NOIDA logo](page_280_image_1_v2.jpg)

**Regression Testing:** The objective of regression testing is to ensure software remains intact. A baseline set of data and scripts will be maintained and executed to verify changes introduced during the release have not “undone” any previous code. Expected results from the baseline are compared to results of the software being regression tested. All discrepancies will be highlighted and accounted for, before testing proceeds to the next level.

**Performance Testing:** Although performance testing is described as a part of system testing, it can be regarded as a distinct level of testing. Performance testing will verify the load, volume, and response times as defined by requirements.

**Load Testing:** Testing an application under heavy loads, such as the testing of a web site under a range of loads to determine at what point the systems response time degrades or fails.

**Installation Testing:** Testing full, partial, or upgrade install/uninstall processes. The installation test for a release will be conducted with the objective of demonstrating production readiness. This test is conducted after the application has been migrated to the client’s site. It will encompass the inventory of configuration items (performed by the application’s System Administration) and evaluation of data readiness, as well as dynamic tests focused on basic system functionality. When necessary, a sanity test will be performed following the installation testing.

**Security/Penetration Testing:** Testing how well the system protects against unauthorized internal or external access, willful damage, etc. This type of testing may require sophisticated testing techniques.

**Recovery/Error Testing:** Testing how well a system recovers from crashes, hardware failures, or other catastrophic problems.

**Acceptance Testing:** During the test scenarios definition, for each of the business scenario, an acceptance criterion is defined. Acceptance criteria include expected behavior of the s/w component and the expected results (data). Expected results form a part of the Exit Criteria. In addition to expected result and behaviors, some conditions are also specified in the exit criteria. They can be:
*   Number of bugs to be discovered for a functional module. This depends on size of the functionality and is an indicator of amount of testing done. If any medium or low-priority errors are outstanding - the implementation risk must be signed off as acceptable by NOIDA and Lead Partner along with consortium partners
*   All High Priority errors from System Test must be fixed and tested by MSI along with consortium partners needs to get the acceptance criteria approved from NOIDA for all the functional components of the system. The Acceptance Criteria for each release into production environment will be agreed upon by MSI along with consortium partners in consultation with NOIDA prior to release from Testing to production environment. After installation, if any bug is reported or there is non-compliance to requirements then a proper procedure should be followed. End-user should report (“Change Request”) to his/her supervisor about the bug that will in turn get forwarded to Project Manager

Noida Safe City Project – Volume 2 – Scope of Work 280

![NOIDA logo](page_281_image_1_v2.jpg)

(PM). PM will forward the List of change request to Lead Partner along with consortium partners. After the bug is fixed, it should be reflected in the production copy after testing it.

**Performance Testing**: The MSI has to test and demonstrate the operational performance requirement as per specification after completion of entire scope. This will be part of acceptance testing. The system will be taken over by owner only after successful operational performance testing. The MSI has to arrange necessary hardware / software to demonstrate the performance testing. MSI should note that NOIDA can appoint a third party agency for conducting any part of above testing procedures (in addition to the testing carried out by the bidder).

## 13. Quality Assurance Methodologies and Practices

Quality assurance (QA) methodologies are crucial in ensuring that projects meet specified requirements and standards throughout their lifecycle. This matrix details various QA methodologies, including procedures, required documentation, compliance standards, testing procedures, and sign-off requirements. Each methodology serves a specific purpose and involves various stakeholders, ensuring that quality is maintained at every stage of the project.

### 1. First Article Inspection (FAI)

**Overview:**

FAI is a critical quality assurance process that evaluates the first produced sample of a product against its design specifications. This inspection ensures that the production process is capable of consistently delivering quality products before large-scale manufacturing begins.

**Importance:**

* Early Detection of Issues: Identifying potential defects or deviations from specifications at the beginning can prevent costly rework or delays later.

* Baseline for Production: Establishes a reference point for quality that future production runs can be compared against.

**Methodology:**

* Planning: Clearly define inspection criteria (e.g., dimensional accuracy, material quality) and develop a schedule for conducting the FAI.

* Execution: Conduct thorough inspections and tests, such as measuring dimensions with calipers and performing functional tests.

* Documentation: Compile an FAI Report that summarizes findings and outlines any corrective actions required.

* Sign-off: Ensure that the Noida Authority, OEM, MSI, and Consultant review and approve the FAI Report to confirm that production can proceed.

**Standard Practice:**

* Inspection Planning: Develop a comprehensive inspection plan detailing acceptance criteria and testing methods.

* Documentation: Maintain thorough records of findings and corrective actions for future reference.

* Stakeholder Engagement: Involve the Noida Authority, OEM, MSI, and Consultant in the FAI process for transparency and consensus on quality standards.

Noida Safe City Project – Volume 2 – Scope of Work 285

![Noida logo](page_286_image_1_v2.jpg)

## 2. Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT)

### Overview:
FAT is a testing phase performed at the manufacturer’s facility to verify that the equipment or systems meet specified requirements before shipping to the project site.

### Importance:
* Quality Assurance Before Shipping: Ensures that equipment is fully functional and meets project specifications, reducing the risk of issues during installation.
* Cost Efficiency: Detecting problems at the factory allows for easier corrections compared to making changes on-site.

### Methodology:
* Preparation: Develop a FAT plan outlining the scope of testing, acceptance criteria, and responsible parties, including the Noida Authority, OEM, MSI, and Consultant.
* Execution: Conduct a series of tests (e.g., performance, safety, functional) to ensure compliance with project specifications.
* Documentation: Create a FAT Report detailing test results and any issues identified, including corrective measures taken.
* Sign-off: Obtain approvals from the Noida Authority, OEM, MSI, and Consultant on the FAT results to facilitate shipment of the equipment.

### Standard Practices:
* Test Procedures: Create detailed test procedures and acceptance criteria for verification.
* Collaboration: Work closely with manufacturers and the Noida Authority, OEM, MSI, and Consultant during the FAT for real-time issue resolution.
* Reporting: Document all test results, including deviations, for future reference.

## 3. Installation & Verification Report (IVR)

### Overview:
The IVR documents the installation process of systems or components, verifying that installations conform to design specifications and meet quality standards.

### Importance:
* Accountability: Provides a formal record of the installation process, serving as a basis for future inspections or audits.
* Verification of Compliance: Ensures that installations are performed correctly, critical for system performance and reliability.

### Methodology:
* Preparation: Create a standardized IVR template to capture necessary installation details (e.g., component specifications, installation conditions).
* Execution: During installation, document each step, including verification of compliance with installation guidelines.
* Documentation: Compile the IVR, noting any issues and how they were resolved during installation.

Noida Safe City Project – Volume 2 – Scope of Work 286

![Noida logo](page_287_image_1_v2.jpg)

- Sign-off: Review the IVR with the Noida Authority, OEM, MSI, and Consultant and obtain signatures to confirm the completion and compliance of the installation.

**Standard Practices:**

- Installation Checklists: Develop checklists to ensure all installation aspects are covered.
- Verification Processes: Conduct step-by-step verification to confirm compliance with design specifications.
- Stakeholder Reviews: Engage the Noida Authority, OEM, MSI, and Consultant in reviewing IVRs to ensure all parties agree on quality.

**4. Site Acceptance Testing (SAT)**

**Overview:**

SAT is conducted after the system is installed at the project site to verify that it operates according to specified requirements in the actual operating environment.

**Importance:**

- Operational Validation: Ensures that the system functions correctly in its intended environment and meets user expectations.
- Final Quality Check: Provides a last opportunity to identify and resolve any issues before final acceptance.

**Methodology:**

- Preparation: Develop a SAT plan that includes the scope of testing, required resources, and acceptance criteria involving the Noida Authority, OEM, MSI, and Consultant.
- Execution: Perform tests in the operational setting, validating all functionalities.
- Documentation: Compile a SAT Report outlining results, any discrepancies, and corrective actions taken.
- Sign-off: Present the SAT Report to the Noida Authority, OEM, MSI, and Consultant and obtain approvals for final acceptance.

**Standard Practices:**

- Test Planning: Develop a comprehensive SAT plan defining scope, criteria, and methods for testing.
- Operational Context: Conduct testing in conditions resembling the intended operational environment for accurate results.
- Issue Resolution: Establish processes for quickly addressing and documenting issues encountered during SAT.

**5. Partial Acceptance Testing (PAT)**

**Overview:**

PAT allows for the acceptance of individual components or systems before the entire project is completed, validating that completed portions meet specifications.

**Importance:**

- Incremental Acceptance: Facilitates phased acceptance of a project, enabling early deployment of functional parts while finalizing remaining components.
- Flexibility: Allows the project to progress in stages, beneficial for time-sensitive deployments.

Noida Safe City Project – Volume 2 – Scope of Work 287

![Noida Authority Logo](page_288_image_1_v2.jpg)

## Methodology:
*   Preparation: Identify components ready for testing and establish criteria for partial acceptance, involving the Noida Authority, OEM, MSI, and Consultant.
*   Execution: Conduct tests on the identified components, verifying that they meet performance and functional specifications.
*   Documentation: Create a PAT Report capturing test results and acceptance confirmations for the partial components.
*   Sign-off: Review and approve the PAT Report with the Noida Authority, OEM, MSI, and Consultant to formalize acceptance.

## Standard Practices:
*   Incremental Testing: Implement testing phases allowing for partial acceptance of completed components.
*   Stakeholder Communication: Keep the Noida Authority, OEM, MSI, and Consultant informed about progress and issues during PAT.
*   Documentation and Reporting: Document each PAT clearly to establish accountability and provide a basis for future testing and acceptance.

## 6. Final Acceptance Testing (FAT)

### Overview:
Final Acceptance Testing is the last step in the quality assurance process, ensuring that the entire system meets contractual specifications and is fully operational before handover.

### Importance:
*   Completion Confirmation: Validates that all components work together seamlessly and meet all project specifications, marking the official project closure.
*   Client Confidence: Provides assurance to the Noida Authority that the project is completed to their expectations and requirements.

### Methodology:
*   Preparation: Develop a comprehensive FAT plan covering all system aspects, including user acceptance criteria and final test scenarios, involving the Noida Authority, OEM, MSI, and Consultant.
*   Execution: Perform final tests to validate overall system readiness and functionality.
*   Documentation: Compile the Final Acceptance Report, detailing results and any outstanding issues.
*   Sign-off: Secure final approval from the Noida Authority, OEM, MSI, and Consultant, marking the official acceptance of the project.

### Standard Practices:
*   Comprehensive Testing: Conduct extensive testing to cover all aspects of the system.
*   Final Reporting: Document all findings and corrections, presenting them to the Noida Authority, OEM, MSI, and Consultant for review.
*   Formal Handover: Ensure all parties sign off on the Final Acceptance Report to officially close the project.

## Detailed Procedures and Testing Metrics

### 1. First Article Inspection (FAI)

*   **Procedures:**
    *   Define Inspection Criteria: Set clear and detailed criteria based on the specifications provided by the design and engineering teams. This includes dimensions, materials, and functional capabilities.
    *   Conduct Inspection: Perform the inspection using appropriate tools and methods. This involves physical measurements, testing for functionality, and visual checks for defects.
    *   Document Findings: All results should be carefully documented in an FAI Report. This report should highlight any discrepancies and outline necessary corrective actions.
*   **Testing Procedures:**
    *   Dimensional Measurements: Use precision measuring tools to verify that critical dimensions are within specified tolerances.
    *   Functional Testing: Assess whether the item performs its intended function as per design specifications.
    *   Visual Inspections: Conduct thorough visual checks for any aesthetic or surface defects.

### 2. Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT)

*   **Procedures:**
    *   Develop FAT Plan: Create a comprehensive plan detailing the scope, testing methods, acceptance criteria, and the roles of various stakeholders during the testing process.
    *   Conduct Site Visit for FAT: Visit the manufacturer's facility to observe the assembly process and evaluate how the system is being built and tested.
        *   Pre-Visit Preparation: Ensure all necessary testing equipment, tools, and documentation are ready for the visit.
        *   Conduct Observations: Assess the production practices, materials used, and assembly quality during the visit.
    *   Execute Planned Tests: Carry out the tests as outlined in the FAT plan, ensuring that all components function as expected.
    *   Document Results: Compile findings in a FAT Report, detailing any identified issues and corrective actions taken.
*   **Testing Procedures:**
    *   Performance Tests: Assess how well the system operates under simulated conditions to ensure it meets the performance specifications.
    *   Safety Tests: Check the system for compliance with safety regulations and standards to mitigate any risks.
    *   Functional Tests: Validate that all operational capabilities are functioning correctly, including control systems and user interfaces.

### 3. Installation & Verification Report (IVR)

*   **Procedures:**

Noida Safe City Project – Volume 2 – Scope of Work 290

![Noida logo](page_291_image_1_v2.jpg)

*   Create Installation Checklist: Develop a comprehensive checklist that outlines all steps required for the installation of equipment and systems.
*   Document Installation Process: Record the installation activities step-by-step, noting any deviations from the planned process and how they were addressed.
*   Conduct Verification: After installation, conduct checks to verify that all components are installed correctly and operate according to specifications.
    *   **Testing Procedures:**
        *   Visual Inspections: Perform thorough inspections to confirm that all components are in place and free from defects.
        *   Compliance Checks: Validate that the installation meets all relevant guidelines, standards, and design specifications.

## 4. Site Acceptance Testing (SAT)

*   **Procedures:**
    *   Prepare SAT Plan: Create a detailed plan that outlines the testing procedures, objectives, expected outcomes, and roles of stakeholders during the testing phase.
    *   Conduct Tests in Operational Environment: Execute tests to validate that the system performs correctly in its intended operational context.
    *   Document Findings: Record all results, including any failures or issues encountered, in the SAT Report.
*   **Testing Procedures:**
    *   Operational Functionality Tests: Verify that the system operates correctly in real-world scenarios and meets performance expectations.
    *   Stress Tests: Assess how the system performs under high-load or extreme conditions to ensure reliability and durability.

## 5. Partial Acceptance Testing (PAT)

*   **Procedures:**
    *   Identify Components for PAT: Select components or systems that have been completed and are ready for testing.
    *   Execute Testing: Conduct tests to evaluate the performance and compliance of the selected components.
    *   Document Acceptance: Record all test results and document any discrepancies in the PAT Report, confirming which components are accepted.
*   **Testing Procedures:**
    *   Component Performance Tests: Verify that each component meets its specified performance criteria.
    *   Functionality Verification: Ensure that each function operates correctly as intended.

## 6. Final Acceptance Testing (FAT)

*   **Procedures:**

Noida Safe City Project – Volume 2 – Scope of Work 291

![Noida logo](page_292_image_1_v2.jpg)

*   Develop Comprehensive FAT Plan: Create a detailed plan encompassing all components and their interactions within the system.
*   Conduct Extensive Testing: Execute thorough tests to confirm that the entire system meets the defined acceptance criteria.
*   Document Results: Record findings and any corrective actions taken in the Final Acceptance Report, which serves as a summary of the entire testing process.
*   **Testing Procedures:**
    *   System Integration Tests: Validate the interoperability and functionality of all system components when integrated.
    *   User Acceptance Tests: Confirm that the system meets user requirements and expectations through testing conducted by end-users.

## Documentation and Compliance Overview

### 1. Documents Required:

*   FAI Report: A comprehensive document summarizing the results of the First Article Inspection, including corrective actions.
*   FAT Plan and Report: Detailed documentation outlining the FAT process and results, including observations from the site visit.
*   IVR Template: A structured document capturing all details regarding the installation and verification processes.
*   SAT Plan and Report: Documentation detailing the procedures and outcomes of Site Acceptance Testing.
*   PAT Report: A document that records the performance and acceptance of individual components.
*   Final Acceptance Report: A comprehensive summary of all testing results and acceptance for final handover.

### 2. Sign-Off Requirements:

Each quality methodology culminates in a sign-off process requiring formal approval from:

*   Noida Authority: The overseeing body responsible for project compliance and acceptance.
*   OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer): The manufacturer providing the equipment or system, ensuring it meets design specifications.
*   Master System Integrator (MSI): The entity integrating various system components and ensuring they work together effectively.
*   Consultant: Project Management Consultant selected by Noida Authority and the expert overseeing the project and ensuring adherence to best practices and standards.
